Thought: Ethers are typically stored under an inert atmosphere to prevent the formation of peroxides. Ethers can react with oxygen in the air to form explosive peroxides, especially upon prolonged exposure. This is why an inert atmosphere, such as nitrogen or argon, is often used to minimize this risk. None of the other options (hydrolysis, oxidation to aldehydes, or polymerization) are common issues with ethers stored under normal conditions.
